title: Vec Get and Length
story: You built a high-score board for your game. The top score is at position 0. But a new player asks: 'What's the 50th highest score?' There are only 3 scores! You need a safe way to look up scores without crashing.
why: `.get(index)` returns `Option[T]` for safe access — no index-out-of-bounds crashes, unlike direct bracket indexing.
analogy: `.get()` is like asking a librarian: 'Do you have book number 42?' The librarian checks the shelf and either hands you the book (Some) or says 'Sorry, we only have 10 books' (None). You never reach for a book that isn't there.
try_it: Create a Vec with 5 fruits. Access index 0, index 4, and index 100. Try accessing index -1 (does XIOM reject negative indices?). Write a loop that prints every element using .get() and .len() together. Then try using `items.get(items.len() - 1)` to get the last element — this is a common pattern.
tips: `.get()` is always safe — it returns `Option[T]`, never crashes on bad indices
Index 0 is the FIRST element, index `.len() - 1` is the LAST element
Combine `.len()` with `.get()` when you need to iterate by index
common_mistakes: Forgetting to match on the Option — `.get()` returns `Option[T]`, not the raw value
Assuming `.get()` removes the item from the Vec — it only reads, the Vec is unchanged
Off-by-one: `.get(3)` on a Vec of length 3 returns `None` because valid indices are 0, 1, 2
